key_insight: EHR-RobustGym shows that clinical AI agents can sound plausible yet fail when EHR evidence is noisy, missing, or inconsistent, and that robustness can be measured and improved with training.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark helps evaluate whether hospital-facing AI can reason safely over real-world records instead of relying on unsupported assumptions.
method: Built on MIMIC-IV with 365K patients, 31 tables, and 500M+ records.
Created 5,486 Clean-Noise pairs across six clinical intents and patient-level/population-level queries.
Tested robustness to record-level, value-level, and query-level noise using interactive SQL/Python execution and outcome verification.
evidence_signal: Across evaluated models, average task success dropped from 62.2% on clean questions to 37.9% on noisy questions, and pass^k consistency at k=4 fell below 50% for most models.
watch_item: Performance gains from this benchmark do not guarantee safe real-world deployment, especially where local data quality, workflow integration, and verification rules differ.
paper_title: EHR-RobustGym: Benchmarking and Training Agents for Robust Clinical Reasoning
